title: Design a Global Video Streaming Platform (YouTube / Netflix)
summary: Design an end-to-end distributed video ingestion, transcoding pipeline, adaptive bitrate streaming, and multi-CDN distribution architecture.
description: Design a planetary-scale video streaming platform capable of serving hundreds of millions of daily active users. The architecture must handle reliable chunked video uploads from creators, orchestrate a distributed GPU-accelerated transcoding pipeline into Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) formats (HLS / MPEG-DASH), deliver video segments via a multi-CDN edge network with sub-1.5s startup latency, and track cross-device playback checkpoints.
functional_requirements: Resumable Chunked Video Uploads: Enable creators to upload multi-gigabyte raw video files with seamless resumption across network disconnections.
Distributed Transcoding Pipeline: Automatically transcode raw footage into multiple resolutions (4K, 1080p, 720p, 480p, 360p) and codecs (H.264, VP9, AV1).
Adaptive Bitrate Streaming (ABR): Stream media using HLS/DASH protocols, dynamically adjusting stream quality based on client device network bandwidth.
Metadata, Search & Catalog: Manage video titles, descriptions, categories, thumbnails, and channel associations with fast catalog querying.
Playback Resumption: Continuously record user playback progress to enable instant resume across smart TVs, mobile apps, and web browsers.
non_functional_requirements: Ultra-low Startup Buffering: P95 video playback startup time strictly under 1.5 seconds.
High Availability & CDN Offload: 99.99% playback availability with >= 95% of video chunk traffic served directly from edge CDN Points of Presence (PoPs).
Transcoding Throughput: Transcode uploaded media within 1.0x of the video runtime (a 10-minute video finishes encoding within 10 minutes).
Durability & Storage Tiering: Master videos and segments must achieve 99.999999999% (11 9s) durability with automated tiering to cold storage (Glacier) for aging content.
Global Scale: Support over 1 billion daily video streams and handle peak global egress bandwidth exceeding 100 Tbps.
key_challenges: Distributed Transcoding Pipeline: Splitting raw videos into Group of Pictures (GOP) chunks, running parallel transcoding tasks across GPU clusters, and assembling unified HLS playlist manifests (.m3u8).
Adaptive Bitrate & Client Buffer Management: Generating multi-bitrate segment variants and tuning chunk duration (2 to 6 seconds) to minimize buffering without excessive HTTP request overhead.
Multi-CDN Edge Steering: Dynamically balancing traffic across multiple CDN vendors (Akamai, Cloudflare, Fastly) using real-time client telemetry to optimize latency and bandwidth costs.

Atomic View Counting on Viral Media: Preventing database lock contention during viral events by accumulating view counts in Redis HyperLogLog / atomic memory counters and asynchronously flushing to persistence.
Cost-effective Storage Lifecycle: Implementing intelligent tiered storage migrating unviewed video renditions to lower-cost object storage while keeping high-demand segments warm in edge memory.

reference_solution.architecture_pattern: Decoupled chunked ingestion pipeline, DAG-based distributed transcoding cluster, Multi-CDN edge delivery network, and polyglot persistence architecture
core_components: Upload Ingestion Service with S3/GCS Multipart Upload and resumable Tus protocol support
Raw Video Staging Bucket triggering asynchronous transcode events via cloud pub/sub
Transcoding Workflow Engine (DAG Orchestrator) dividing videos into GOP slices and scheduling worker jobs
Transcoding GPU Fleet encoding parallel slices into H.264/AV1 bitrates and generating HLS manifests
Master Segment Object Storage storing finalized .m3u8 playlists and 4-second .ts/.m4s video chunks
Multi-CDN Edge Distribution Layer caching video chunks at ISP edge nodes closest to consumers
Metadata & Catalog Service (PostgreSQL) storing video metadata, tags, and channel relations
User Playback Progress Store (Cassandra / DynamoDB) persisting frequent watch progress updates with low latency
reference_solution.hls_segmentation_strategy: Raw video is split into independent 4-second chunks at keyframe boundaries (I-frames), encoded in parallel across 5 standard resolutions, and compiled into a master HLS index manifest referencing bitrate variants.
reference_solution.cdn_traffic_steering: A smart DNS / latency-based router steers playback requests to the optimal CDN provider based on real-time end-user telemetry and provider SLA health.
